renderer_changes: Flag (no change requested): pose-skeleton-3d.js line 214 comment claims +90 = supine, but actual rotX(+90) makes body face-down (prone). The worker-D task description repeats this incorrect convention. Correct convention: +90 = prone, -90 = supine.
regression_risk: HIGH — globalTilt sign flip (-20 to +85) is a dramatic change (body goes from mostly-upright to horizontal prone). Pose silhouette completely changes. However, this matches the description intent (hands-and-knees on bench). Wrists still not at y=-0.8 (rig constraint) but body is now correctly horizontal face-down.
rationale: Worker-D task description claims globalTilt ~-90 (prone) but VERIFIED via rotX math that actual code: +90 = prone (face-down), -90 = supine (on back). p10-bench-s10 (Lie on your back) uses globalTilt -85 (supine) confirming. So all-fours prone needs globalTilt +85..+90. Fix: globalTilt 85 (body horizontal face-down). With original R leg config (rightHip -12, rightKnee 10), the R foot ends up at y=0.04 (barely above hip level) — but instructions say Extend one leg straight back and slightly up off the bench. Fix: rightHip -40 (thigh more extended back in body frame → leg points more up in world after prone rotation) — derived R foot at (0.43, 0.41, -0.60), y=0.41 (up off bench ✓), z=-0.60 (behind body ✓). L leg unchanged (leftHip 118, leftKnee 130 — L thigh forward in body frame → down in world, knee below hips, foot below body). Spine -30 preserved (back arch in body frame). Wrists after prone rotation: y=-0.28, -0.22 (below hips, near bench surface — closer to ground but not at y=-0.8 due to rig constraint: hip origin fixed at y=0, arms can extend down ~0.7 max).
